## Purpose

This notebook documents the exploratory assessment of relationships among environmental variables and the selection of candidate predictors for the subsequent logistic regression models. Correlations and boosted regression trees (BRTs) are evaluated using the combined R-M2 and R-M4 dataset. The BRT response is the continuous HESY2 EQR; the two river types are modelled separately in the subsequent analysis.

The input is a prepared dataset containing site-averaged environmental and biological observations for the two river types. The preparation of this dataset is described in the repository README. 

The original BRT settings are retained. 

The `dismo` functions are called with `dismo::`, without attaching the package, to avoid masking `dplyr` functions.



```{r setup}
# ---- Required packages ----
# dplyr   : Data manipulation and filtering
# ggplot2 : Data visualisation
# readr   : Reading and writing CSV files
# here    : Project-relative file paths
# dismo   : Boosted regression tree modelling (gbm.step)
# gbm     : Boosted regression modelling engine used by dismo

required_packages <- c(
  "dplyr",
  "ggplot2",
  "readr",
  "here",
  "dismo",
  "gbm"
)

# ---- Load packages used without :: ----

library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

# Other packages are accessed using package::function()
```


## 1. Input data

Observations with missing HESY2 or DO values, or DO concentrations ≥20 mg L⁻¹, were excluded

```{r getdata}

input_file <- here::here("Data", "Processed", "Greek_RM2_RM4_SiteMeans.csv")
stopifnot(file.exists(input_file))

candidate_predictors <- c(
  "Cond", "N_NO3", "N_NH4", "P_PO4", "DO",
  "BOD", "Mean.Flow", "HMS", "ICTypeF"
)

required_vars <- c("ICType", "HESY2", setdiff(candidate_predictors, "ICTypeF"))

dat <- readr::read_csv(input_file, show_col_types = FALSE)
missing_vars <- setdiff(required_vars, names(dat))
if (length(missing_vars)) {
  stop("Missing input columns: ", paste(missing_vars, collapse = ", "))
}

dat <- dat %>%
  filter(ICType %in% c("R-M2", "R-M4"), !is.na(HESY2), DO < 20) %>%
  mutate(ICTypeF = factor(ICType, levels = c("R-M2", "R-M4")))

output_dir <- here::here("Outputs", "Figures")
dir.create(output_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
```

## 2. Correlations

The scatterplot matrix shows pairwise relationships among HESY2 and the numerical environmental variables. Upper panels show absolute Pearson correlations, calculated using available pairs of observations. River type is omitted from this matrix because it is categorical; it is retained as a predictor in the BRT.

```{r correlations, fig.width=8.5, fig.height=8.5}
cor_vars <- c(
  "HESY2", "Cond", "N_NO3", "N_NH4", "P_PO4",
  "DO", "BOD", "Mean.Flow", "HMS"
)

panel_cor <- function(x, y, ...) {
  old_par <- par("usr")
  on.exit(par(usr = old_par))
  par(usr = c(0, 1, 0, 1))
  r <- suppressWarnings(cor(x, y, use = "pairwise.complete.obs"))
  label <- if (is.finite(r)) sprintf("%.2f", abs(r)) else "NA"
  text(0.5, 0.5, label, cex = 1.1)
}

plot_correlations <- function() {
  pairs(
    dat[, cor_vars],
    lower.panel = panel.smooth,
    upper.panel = panel_cor
  )
}

plot_correlations()

png(file.path(output_dir, "FigS2_Predictor_Correlations.png"),
    width = 9, height = 9, units = "in", res = 300)
plot_correlations()
dev.off()
```

## 3. Boosted regression tree screening

A Gaussian BRT is fitted to the continuous HESY2 EQR using the numerical stressors and river type as candidate predictors. Observations with missing HESY2 values are excluded. Missing predictor values are not explicitly removed before fitting the BRT. The model uses tree complexity 3, learning rate 0.003 and bag fraction 0.5, with random seed 123. This is a screening model: no BRT simplification is undertaken.


```{r brt-fit}
# Keep the response first, as required by gbm.step(gbm.y = 1).
brt_data <- dat %>%
  select(all_of(c("HESY2", candidate_predictors))) %>%
  as.data.frame()

# Document sample sizes
cat("BRT observations by river type:\n")
print(brt_data %>% count(ICTypeF, name = "N"))
cat("Total observations:", nrow(brt_data), "\n")

set.seed(123)
brt_model <- dismo::gbm.step(
  data = brt_data,
  gbm.x = candidate_predictors,
  gbm.y = 1,
  family = "gaussian",
  tree.complexity = 3,
  learning.rate = 0.003,
  bag.fraction = 0.5
)

if (is.null(brt_model)) {
  stop("BRT fitting did not produce a model. Review gbm.step output.")
}

explained_deviance <- with(
  brt_model$self.statistics,
  (mean.null - mean.resid) / mean.null
)

importance <- summary(brt_model, plotit = FALSE)

cat("Observations:", nrow(brt_data), "\n")
cat("Explained deviance:", round(explained_deviance, 3), "\n")
print(importance)

table_dir <- here::here("Outputs", "Tables")
dir.create(table_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
readr::write_csv(importance, file.path(table_dir, "BRT_Relative_Influence.csv"))
```


### Relative influence of predictors

Relative influence is expressed as a percentage and sums to 100 across candidate predictors.

```{r brt-importance, fig.width=7, fig.height=5}
p_importance <- ggplot(
  importance,
  aes(x = reorder(var, -rel.inf), y = rel.inf)
) +
  geom_col(fill = "skyblue") +
  labs(
    title = "EQR HESY2 :relative Importance by Variable",
    subtitle = paste0("Explained deviance: ",
                      round(explained_deviance, 2)),
    x = "Variable",
    y = "Relative Importance"
  ) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 12)

p_importance

ggsave(
  filename = file.path(output_dir, "Fig3_BRT_Relative_Influence.png"),
  plot = p_importance,
  width = 7, height = 5, units = "in", dpi = 300,
  bg = "white"
)
```
